newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM sees new cabinet approved Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM sees new cabinet approved Thursday.

text.p: Slovenia's prime minister- designate , Janez Drnovsek , said on Wednesday he expected the parliament to approve his new cabinet on Thursday, almost three months after inconclusive November 10 general elections.
"I expect parliament will approve the government tomorrow," Drnovsek told a news conference.
The vote, which may be preceded by a debate, will start at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT).
Drnovsek said he would not replace any of the 18 ministerial candidates although six had not been approved by the parliamentary hearing committee.
"The government has been composed well," Drnovsek said, but added he would continue to try to form a broader coalition in the future.

Among key posts, finance minister nominee Mitja Gaspari and interior minister candidate Polonca Dobrajc failed to gain support, while foreign minister candidate Zoran Thaler and economic affairs nominee Metod Dragonja gained approval.
Drnovsek, head of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and prime minister since April 1992, formed a coalition with a one- vote majority 12 days ago.
Apart from his Liberal Democrats, the government comprises former communists the United List of Social Democrats, the pensioners' party Desus and the Nationalist Party.
But three rightist parties of the so-called "Spring" alliance, which together hold 44 out of 90 parliamentary seats, are expected to vote against Drnovsek's government line-up.
If the alliance succeeds in voting down Drnovsek, the prime minister must present a changed government list within 10 days.
The new government will be Slovenia's third since independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
